props.title: Star Wars
props.initialSlug: A farm boy's journey to save a galaxy far, far away

sections.content: Star Wars revolutionized blockbuster filmmaking by fusing Flash Gordon serials, Kurosawa samurai epics, and Joseph Campbell's hero's journey into a groundbreaking space fantasy. George Lucas created an instantly iconic universe where lived-in technology met mystical forces. The practical effects from Industrial Light & Magic set new standards - the Death Star trench run still thrills 45+ years later. The film's DNA shows up everywhere from Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) to The Last Starfighter (1984). Most crucially, John Williams' neo-romantic score brought back sweeping orchestral themes when minimalist scores dominated.

sections.content: The film's massive success transformed Hollywood. Alien (1979) and Blade Runner (1982) built on its lived-in future aesthetic. The merchandising empire revolutionized movie marketing - everything from The Lord of the Rings (2001) to Frozen (2013) follows this model. Lucas' decision to retain merchandising rights instead of a higher salary proved historically lucrative. ILM's innovations led directly to modern CGI, seen in everything from Jurassic Park (1993) to the Marvel films. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

Beyond technical innovation, Star Wars cemented the modern blockbuster template. Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977) and Superman (1978) followed its mix of spectacle and mythology. The film's optimistic tone contrasted with '70s cinema's gritty realism, paving the way for the crowd-pleasing adventures of Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981) and Back to the Future (1985). Even recent films like Dune (2021) still work from Lucas' hero's journey blueprint.
